question.text: Sensitivity analysis in quantitative research involves:

answer.text: Testing only one variable at a time
Understanding the impact of changes in assumptions on valuations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.83, analysts use sensitivity analysis and simulations to understand the impact of changes in assumptions on the valuations they undertake. Per p.239, sensitivity analysis studies how the valuation changes when a critical variable changes, typically by varying one variable at a time while holding the others constant. The Trap: The technique does not determine exact future prices; it shows a range based on assumption changes, and per p.239 it is conducted by changing one variable at a time rather than multiple variables simultaneously. Note: The definitions used here are taken directly from p.83 (impact of assumption changes on valuations) and p.239 (one-variable-at-a-time approach).
